summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 19.2 to Angular 20.3 with `ng update @angular/core@20 @angular/cli@20`, followed by @ngrx/* to 20.1.0 for the peer range. This hop needed no hand-written code fixes: the CLI migrations rewrote `moduleResolution` to 'bundler', pinned the v19 schematics naming defaults in angular.json, and swapped the one `TestBed.get` call for `TestBed.inject`. Install (clean, no --legacy-peer-deps), `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` all pass; tests still fail exactly as at baseline for the same pre-existing angular.json reason.
changes: ng update @angular/core@20 @angular/cli@20 bumped all @angular/* runtime packages to 20.3.34 and @angular/cli / @angular-devkit/build-angular to 20.3.41.

The CLI migration 'Update workspace generation defaults to maintain previous style guide behavior' appended a root `schematics` block to angular.json (component/directive/service `type` and `typeSeparator: "."` for guard/interceptor/module/pipe/resolver). Angular 20 changes the default generated file naming (drops the `.component`-style suffix); this block keeps future `ng generate` output in the existing naming style, so no existing file is renamed.
The CLI migration changed `moduleResolution` from "node" to "bundler" in tsconfig.json. Required direction for v20 tooling; the build and SSR build both resolve cleanly with it.

The core migration replaced `TestBed.get(EmployeeService)` with `TestBed.inject(EmployeeService)` in src/app/services/employee.service.spec.ts. `TestBed.get` was deprecated since v9 and is removed in v20.

Bumped all five @ngrx/* packages from 19.2.1 to 20.1.0. Required: @ngrx 19 peers on `@angular/core: ^19.0.0`, which makes a clean install unresolvable against Angular 20. As in the previous hop the ngrx CLI run died after writing package.json with 'Cannot find module @angular-devkit/core', but @ngrx ships no 19_0_0/20_0_0 migrations (newest on disk are 18_0_0-beta for both store and effects), so nothing was skipped.
typescript stays at ~5.8.3 and zone.js at ~0.15.1: both already satisfy Angular 20.3's requirements, so the update command left them alone.
rxjs stays at ^6.6.7. Angular 20.3's peer range is still `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0` and @ngrx 20 accepts `^6.5.3 || ^7.5.0`, so rxjs 7 is still not forced by this hop.

The other CLI migrations (provideServerRendering import move, withRoutes/provideServerRouting, default karma config removal) and core migrations (DOCUMENT import move, InjectFlags, BootstrapContext) all reported no changes: none of those APIs are used here.

Declined the optional `use-application-builder` migration once more. The webpack `browser`/`server` builders are deprecated but still functional in Angular 20 (verified: both `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` pass), and switching builders would rework the SSR/aspnet-prerendering setup — out of scope for a behaviour-preserving hop, but see followups: it becomes mandatory at v21.
Declined the optional `control-flow-migration` and `router-current-navigation` migrations: the former is a cosmetic template rewrite, and the app never calls `Router.getCurrentNavigation`.
Restored the trailing newline on package.json that the ng update rewrite dropped.

package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified by deleting node_modules and running a plain `npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps needed), then `npm run build`, `npm run build:ssr` and the test command.
manual_followups: `npm run test` still fails exactly as at baseline: angular.json's test target lists "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so webpack reports a load error and karma aborts before any spec runs. Left untouched to keep this hop to the upgrade; it keeps hiding real test breakage in every later hop and is worth fixing on its own.

The webpack `browser` and `server` builders this project still uses are removed in Angular 21. The `use-application-builder` migration (esbuild `application` builder) is therefore the main blocker for the next hop and must be done there, together with rethinking the `build:ssr` target and the aspnet-prerendering server entry.

Karma/jasmine are also on the way out: Angular 20 deprecates the karma test builder, and the test setup here (karma 6.4, jasmine-core 3.10, karma-coverage-istanbul-reporter, @types/jasminewd2) is stale. Expect to move to the `application`-builder test target (or Vitest/Web Test Runner) when the builder migration above happens.
angular.json now carries a root `schematics` block solely to preserve pre-v20 generated-file naming. If the project is happy to adopt Angular 20's new naming, that block can be deleted.
`HTTP_INTERCEPTORS` is still imported in src/app/app.module.ts but unused. Safe to delete; left alone to keep the diff small.

Every component still carries an explicit `standalone: false` from the v19 hop. The real fix is to migrate the app to standalone components and drop the AppModule, which is the default style from v19 on.
rxjs is still 6.6.7. Angular 20 and @ngrx 20 both still accept it, but rxjs 6 is end-of-life; check the peer range again at v21.

The SSR entry still looks like dead code: Startup.cs uses UseSpa/UseAngularCliServer and never UseSpaPrerendering, and aspnet-prerendering is a 2018-era package. Removing the server target and aspnet-prerendering would also simplify the v21 builder migration.
add-employee.component.ts still uses the Untyped* form classes from the v14 opt-out; adopting typed reactive forms is still open.
`useDefineForClassFields: false` is still set in tsconfig.json from the v15 migration; a person should decide whether the app can move to the standard `true` behaviour.

`npm run lint` is still broken from the v13 hop: the tslint architect targets were deleted and nothing replaced them. The project should move to @angular-eslint and drop tslint/codelyzer from optionalDependencies.
angular.json still carries `defaultConfiguration: ""` on the build and server targets from the v12 migration.
node-sass 4.x still fails to build its native binding on modern Node and is skipped as an optional dependency; it is unused by the build but should be dropped or replaced with `sass`.
core-js is still pinned at ^2.6.5 and @types/node at ^12, both far behind the Node 22 toolchain this hop runs on.
The app still uses the old `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` directives rather than the built-in control flow. Not adopted on purpose; Angular 20 supports both.
`npm install` still reports 69 vulnerabilities, almost all from the stale optionalDependencies (protractor, tslint, node-sass, ts-node 5) rather than from Angular itself.
The Browserslist config still lists browsers outside Angular 20's support window (kaios, op_mini, and_qq, and_uc, ...), producing warnings on every build. Harmless, but the list should be trimmed.
